data.stem: Which committee examines the CAG's audit reports on public expenditure and has had an Opposition chairman by convention since 1967?
data.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee examines the CAG's audit reports and, by convention since 1967, its chairman comes from the Opposition, so option A is correct. The Estimates Committee reviews budget estimates, the Committee on Public Undertakings reviews public enterprises, and the Business Advisory Committee allots House time, so B, C and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: What is the total strength of a Department-Related Standing Committee, split by House?
options: Thirty-one: twenty-one Lok Sabha seats and ten Rajya Sabha seats
Thirty: twenty Lok Sabha seats and ten Rajya Sabha seats
Twenty-two: fifteen Lok Sabha seats and seven Rajya Sabha seats
Fifteen: ten Lok Sabha seats and five Rajya Sabha seats
data.explanation: The DRSC composition is 31 seats split 21 and 10, so option A is right. Option B corresponds to the SC and ST panel, option C to the Public Accounts Committee and option D to the Offices of Profit committee, so B, C and D are incorrect for the DRSCs.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Estimates Committee:
1. All of its members are drawn from the Lok Sabha.
2. It examines the budget estimates before Parliament votes on them.
3. Its chairman is generally drawn from the ruling party.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so option A is right: all 30 members come from the Lok Sabha, and the Speaker generally appoints a ruling-party chairman. Statement 2 is wrong because the committee examines estimates only after they are voted, so options B and D include that error, while option C leaves out a correct statement.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which committee is NOT one of the three financial committees of Parliament?
data.explanation: The Committee on Government Assurances tracks promises ministers make on the floor and belongs to the scrutiny group, so option D is the NOT answer. The Public Accounts Committee, the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings are the three financial committees, so A, B and C are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Under which statute was the Public Accounts Committee first set up in 1921?
data.explanation: The Public Accounts Committee was first set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act of 1919, so option A is right. The 1935 Act, the 1909 Indian Councils Act and the 1858 Act are not the source of this committee, so options B, C and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Who recommended the setting up of the first post-independence Estimates Committee in 1950?
data.explanation: John Mathai, the finance minister at the time, recommended the first post-independence Estimates Committee, so option C is correct. Krishna Menon's committee led to the Committee on Public Undertakings, Ashok Chanda was a former CAG who wrote on administration, and Veerappa Moily headed a later administrative reforms commission, so A, B and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which public-enterprise watchdog emerged in 1964 following Krishna Menon's recommendations?
data.explanation: The Krishna Menon panel's suggestion produced the Committee on Public Undertakings in 1964, so option C is correct. The Public Accounts Committee dates from 1921, the Estimates Committee's first post-independence form from 1950, and the Committee of Privileges handles breaches of privilege, so A, B and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Who is the ex-officio President of the Indian Parliamentary Group?
options: Leader of the House in Lok Sabha
data.explanation: Presiding over the IPG by virtue of office is the Lok Sabha's Speaker, so option D is correct. The Rajya Sabha Chairman does not hold the IPG presidency, since only the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha serves as a vice-president, and the Prime Minister and the Leader of the House hold no office in the IPG, so A, C and B are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Parliamentary Group:
1. Former members of Parliament may join it as associate members with limited rights.
2. The Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha is its ex-officio Secretary-General.
3. It was formed in 1960 under a motion of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so option C is right. Statement 3 is wrong because the IPG was formed in 1949 under a motion of the Constituent Assembly, not in 1960 by Rajya Sabha, so options A, B and D each contain that error.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which committee recommends whether holders of certain offices should be disqualified from being elected as members of Parliament?
options: Joint Committee on Offices of Profit
data.explanation: The Joint Committee on Offices of Profit examines the composition of bodies appointed by governments and recommends disqualification where needed, so option B is correct. The Committee of Privileges handles breaches of privilege, the Committee on Petitions examines petitions, and the Ethics Committee enforces the code of conduct, so A, C and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which standing committee enforces the code of conduct for members of Parliament and examines cases of misconduct?
options: Committee on Papers Laid on the Table
data.explanation: The Ethics Committee enforces the members' code of conduct and examines misconduct, so option B is correct. The Committee of Privileges handles breaches of privilege, the Papers Laid committee checks the form of papers, and the Rules Committee deals with House procedure, so A, C and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: In which year was the Lok Sabha's Ethics Committee constituted?
data.explanation: The Lok Sabha Ethics Committee was constituted in 2000, so option C is correct. The 1997 date applies to the Rajya Sabha committee, while 1993 and 2004 are years of the DRSC system, so options A, B and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: What happens to a Department-Related Standing Committee member who is later appointed a minister?
options: He or she stays on as a non-voting member
He or she becomes the committee's chairman
He or she ceases to be a member of the committee
He or she continues only until the committee's report is adopted
data.explanation: A minister cannot be a DRSC member, so a sitting member who becomes a minister ceases to be a member, and option C is correct. The chapter gives no basis for options A, B or D, which describe a non-voting seat, a chairmanship and a term tied to the report, so each is incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about how Department-Related Standing Committees handle demands for grants:
1. Their reports may suggest cut motions in the Lok Sabha.
2. They consider the demands before the House votes on them.
3. Each ministry gets a separate report on its demands.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct, so option A is right: the committees consider demands before the vote and submit a separate report for each ministry. Statement 1 is wrong because their reports must not suggest cut motions, so options B, C and D each include that error.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which subject lies outside the proper remit of a Department-Related Standing Committee?
options: Day-to-day administration of the concerned ministry
Long-term national policy documents placed before the Houses
data.explanation: Day-to-day administration is excluded from DRSC work, so option B is correct. Bills referred to a committee, annual reports of ministries and long-term policy documents are all within its functions, so A, C and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Who chairs a consultative committee attached to a particular ministry?
options: The Minister or Minister of State in charge of that ministry
The senior-most member of the committee
The Secretary of the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
data.explanation: The minister or minister of state in charge of the ministry chairs its consultative committee, so option B is correct. The Speaker, the senior-most member and the Secretary of the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs do not chair these committees, so A, C and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Within what limits does the membership of a consultative committee fall?
data.explanation: A consultative committee has a minimum of 10 and a maximum of 30 members, so option A is right. The other ranges do not match that rule: option B's maximum is too high, option C's minimum is too low, and option D's range is the size of a DRSC, not a consultative committee.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which Lok Sabha committee is chaired by the Deputy Speaker?
options: Committee on Absence of Members from the Sittings of the House
Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions
data.explanation: The Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions is chaired by the Deputy Speaker, so option D is correct. The Business Advisory Committee and the Rules Committee are chaired by the Speaker as ex-officio chairman, and the Absence committee is not chaired by the Deputy Speaker, so A, C and B are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which Lok Sabha committee handles leave applications from members and checks long unauthorised absences?
options: Committee on Absence of Members from the Sittings of the House
data.explanation: The Committee on Absence of Members considers leave applications and examines members absent for 60 days or more without permission, so option D is correct. The Rules Committee handles procedure, the House Committee handles accommodation and amenities, and the General Purposes Committee advises on House affairs, so A, B and C are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which statute underpins the Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of MPs?
options: Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952
Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954
data.explanation: The statute behind that joint committee is the 1954 law on MPs' salary, allowances and pension, so option D is right. The 1952 law deals with ministers, the 1935 Act is older and the 1951 Act concerns elections, so A, B and C are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Who appoints the President of each Parliamentary Friendship Group?
data.explanation: Naming the head of each Friendship Group falls to the Lok Sabha Speaker, so option B is right. The President of India, the Rajya Sabha Chairman and the Prime Minister have no role in choosing that office-holder, so A, C and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: How long must an MP have been a member of the IPG before being included in an Indian parliamentary delegation abroad?
data.explanation: Only members of at least six months' standing in the IPG, measured when the delegation is formed, may be included, so option B is correct. Three months, one year and two years do not match that rule, so options A, C and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which international body is the Indian Parliamentary Group the National Group of?
data.explanation: The IPG acts as India's National Group of the Inter-Parliamentary Union, so option A is correct. The CPA is the body whose main Indian branch the IPG runs, not the one it is the National Group of, while the UN General Assembly and the ILO are not associations of parliaments, so B, C and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Roughly how many parliamentarians and parliamentary staff belong to the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association?
data.explanation: The CPA has about 17,000 parliamentarians and parliamentary staff, so option B is correct. The other figures understate or overstate that membership by a wide margin, so options A, C and D are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which item is NOT among the three audit reports the CAG submits to the President for Parliament?
data.explanation: The CAG submits three audit reports, on appropriation accounts, finance accounts and public undertakings, so a report on defence procurement is not one of them and option D is the NOT answer. Options A, B and C are the three genuine reports, so each is incorrect as an answer.
data.label: practice
